title: Static imports versus normal imports
answer: A normal import brings a type name into scope, such as `java.util.List`, while a static import brings static members of a type into scope so they can be referenced without the declaring class name. AeroTopo's `LearningLabTest` normally imports classes and also uses `import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.*;` so assertion methods can be called directly. Static imports improve readability for well-known utility methods but can hurt clarity when overused or when names collide.
